Subject: Follow-up: deployment mode & pricing (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the excellent discovery session earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Recap:
- Primary use case: real-time summarization + question answering for customer support transcripts (batch and live ingestion).
- Traffic profile: expected steady-state 50 qps during peak, spiky bursts to 120 qps for short windows.
- Latency target: 150-200ms p50 on short chats; p95 under 400ms.
- Data concerns: some PII, regulated EU customers down the line — interested in VPC or on-prem options for regulated workloads.

Deployment mode considerations (what we discussed):
- Hosted API: fastest to launch, per-token pricing, automatic scaling — good if you want minimal ops and elastic bursts.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): predictable throughput, reserved GPU pools, monthly commits — better for stable high-throughput and cost predictability.
- Private VPC / on-prem: needed for strict data residency/compliance, higher setup & recurring infra costs but full control.

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you confirm the 50 qps steady / 120 qps burst estimate and the percent of requests that are short (<=256 tokens)?
2) Any hard constraints on data residency or required compliance (SOC2/Pci/Sap)?
3) I’ll loop in Neha (solutions engineer) and Marissa (pricing) to produce a short cost model for each deployment mode — per-token estimate for Hosted vs monthly reserved capacity estimate for Dedicated vs an outline for Private VPC TCO.

If that looks right I’ll aim to get a short, scannable cost comparison across the three options by EOD Friday.

Best,

Hi Sam / Aditya —

Thanks for the details — I put together a concise cost comparison below based on the numbers you shared. Keeping it scannable so you can share with procurement. I’ll follow up with a short spreadsheet if you want line-item math.

Option A — Hosted API (per-token)
- Assumptions: 50 qps steady (~4.32M requests/month), 70% short (avg 200 tokens), 25% mid (avg 600 tokens), 5% long (avg 1200 tokens) => ~1.5B tokens/month
- Example pricing: $0.0008 per input token + $0.0012 per output token (illustrative) => ballpark $1,800–$3,200/month depending on prompt sizes and output lengths (we’ll refine once we see sample prompt/output lengths).
- Pros: fastest to launch, auto-scaling, zero infra ops.
- Cons: less predictable billing at scale; higher unit cost for very high sustained throughput.

Option B — Dedicated (reserved capacity)
- Assumptions: 2 reserved GPU clusters sized to sustain baseline 50 qps with burst capacity for 120 qps (autoscaling/burst).
- Pricing model: monthly reserved commit + metered overages. Example: $45k–$70k/month for committed capacity covering baseline (depends on model family / quantization). Overages billed at reduced per-token equivalent.
- Pros: predictable unit economics, SLAs, lower unit cost at scale.
- Cons: requires monthly commitment; provisioning lead time for larger clusters.

Option C — Private VPC / On‑prem
- Assumptions: Dedicated VPC deployment with customer-managed infra. Initial onboarding & deployment fee + recurring infra and support.
- Pricing example: one-time integration/setup $40k–$80k + annual platform license / support $180k/year + expected infra costs (varies by region).
- Pros: full control for compliance/data residency; best for regulated EU deployments.
- Cons: higher TCO, longer setup.

Next steps I propose:
1) If you want, we’ll produce a 1‑page ROI / cost spreadsheet that converts Hosted per-token to an expected monthly $ figure using the RFP sample and then show Dedicated commit break-even points.
2) Flag any hard constraints (e.g., EU-only for some customers) so we can show a hybrid approach (Hosted for US pilot + Private VPC for EU enterprise).
3) If procurement prefers an anchor number for negotiations, we can propose a draft term sheet for a 12‑month commit and expected SLAs.

Happy to refine — we can sync Monday if that works.

—Marissa Cole
Pricing & GTM Operations | Redwood Inference
